doctrine: The Attention Stack is a systematic, repeatable system for content production, distribution, and audience-building in photography. Core doctrine: 1) Interest Media (views > followers, follower count is vanity metric); 2) Organic as R&D, paid amplifies only validated winners; 3) Document, don't create (rough footage 10x outperforms polished content); 4) Hook decides everything (first 1-3 seconds); 5) Volume over polish (4-15 posts/day); 6) Platform-native or invisible (one idea, seven platform adaptations); 7) Brand is last moat (generic equals invisible in AI era). PAC Framework runs three variables in parallel: Platforms (7-9 platform footprint, underpriced platforms prioritized), Algorithms (review monthly, match format preferences), Culture (14-day freshness floor on trends/audio). Creative Validation Workflow: produce 5-30 variations, organic test zero-spend, 7-day lookback, identify top 5 percent, amplify 80 percent of paid budget to validated winners only, iterate. Budget shift from 80/20 (media/creative) to 50/50 flips where spend goes. 7x7 Workflow: batch capture daily (voice notes, shoot footage, process video), AI processing into seven platform-specific cutdowns, distribute 7+ daily, track performance. Operating targets: 1-3 core pieces daily, 7-15 platform cutdowns daily, 30-90 core pieces monthly. 80/20 content split: 80 percent structural (niche content, core work), 20 percent cultural (trends, off-niche, discovery engine). Hook Factory treats hooks as separate production track with 5 categories: contrarian statement, specific result, question the viewer has, before-and-after promise, visual surprise. Live commerce combines face-to-face trust with internet reach. Monetization in sequence: Pebbles ($15-99), Small Boulders ($99-499), Medium Boulders ($499-2,000), Large Boulders ($2,000+). Niche of One strategy: intersection of two unrelated skills, non-competitive, higher pricing power. 100-Video Rule: produce 100 pieces authentically across full range, ignore view counts, then identify algorithm-identified intersection by clustering. AI integration via context injection (5-13 min voice note describing business, then paste as system context). Operators sequence in seven phases: Phase 1 Audit, Phase 2 Learn (50-100 hrs hands-on AI), Phase 3 Produce (7x7 daily), Phase 4 Test/Listen (continuous Creative Validation Workflow), Phase 5 Amplify (top 5 percent paid), Phase 6 Monetize (month 3 forward, first pebble), Phase 7 Iterate (permanent monthly reviews). Psychology layer: Elephant Meeting (brand control illusion solved by participating), 9 PM-midnight window (asymmetric upside for day-job photographers), Cynicism Tax (Maybe Filter: test 90 days with capped loss), Practical Optimism (grounded in market verdict), Total Views reframe (track views across 8 platforms, not followers). Metrics that matter: view velocity (views per hour first 24 hours vs baseline), save and share rate (2-5 percent normal, 5 percent+ compounding), comment depth (short/medium/threaded signal), follower-to-view ratio (Interest Media when >1). Platform specifics: LinkedIn (image posts, B2B, 7-9 AM post time, 2-hr engagement window), Instagram Reels (portfolio, saves/shares matter, product tagging, 4-7 per week), TikTok (organic discovery, watch time + shares primary, 2-5 per week minimum), YouTube Shorts (long-tail index, cross-post Reels, feeds AI training), Facebook (overlooked, 1-second videos, older spending demographic, community groups underused), Substack (email list ownership, weekly cadence, monetize at 5,000+ subscribers), Whatnot/TikTok Live (live commerce, 80/20 education/pitch structure, local-to-national via shippable products). Single-platform depth alternative: valid when volume model burns out and business needs smaller high-value audience (4-7 Instagram posts/week or 1 YouTube video/week or 1 weekly newsletter, none else). Community over virality: track comment depth, repeat buyers, referral rate, open rates on newsletters. Two-phase approach: 6-12 months volume to build library and identify Niche of One via 100-Video Rule, then shift 70-80 percent effort to single platform for depth, maintain minimum presence elsewhere. Closing paradox: system is not complicated, it is demanding. Requirement is 12 months daily practice before compounding visible. Gap between photographers stuck below revenue ceiling and those at ceiling: the photographers at ceiling have built this systematic attention layer.

prompts: AI context injection: '5-13 minute voice note describing your business in detail: niche, audience, voice, goals this quarter, last three shoots, clients, pricing tiers, current constraints. Transcribe and paste at session start before any other prompt.'

Weekly content plan: 'Using the business context above, propose a content plan for the coming week. Include: 1 core theme, 7 daily post concepts (platform-specific), 3 hook variations, 1 cultural off-niche post. Format as table: Platform, day, content type, hook, body summary, call to action.'
Hook variation generator: '10 hook variations (first 3 seconds video or first line caption): 3 contrarian, 2 specific-result, 2 question, 2 before-and-after, 1 visual-surprise. [paste draft]'

Platform cutdowns: 'Turn this voice note into: 1) LinkedIn image post 6-8 line caption, 2) Instagram Reel script 30 sec with hook/CTA, 3) TikTok script 45 sec with trending audio suggestions, 4) YouTube Shorts script 50 sec SEO title, 5) X thread 5-7 posts, 6) Substack section 300 words. Keep my voice, do not flatten.'
Comment/DM synthesis: 'Synthesize 50 recent comments/DMs: top 3 recurring questions, top 3 objections, top 3 unmet needs, 5 content ideas to address. [paste 50 items]'

operating_rules: Interest Media law: follower count is vanity metric, track views per post. Viewer's behavior (not follow status) drives algorithm.
Organic R&D law: organic content is laboratory at zero cost to be wrong. Paid media never precedes organic validation.
Document law: rough phone footage from setup beats cinematic video 10:1. Documentation reads as person, polish reads as ad.
Hook law: first 1-3 seconds decides if next 30 happen. 5-20x view delta between best and worst hook.
Volume law: 4-15 posts per day beats any burst. Consistency over 12 months compounds. One long-form recording produces 7+ usable clips.
Platform-native law: never repurpose unchanged. One core idea, seven platform-specific adaptations. Native outperforms repurposed 3-5x on non-native platform.
Brand moat law: 'Portrait photographer LA' returns list. 'Bryceden Jones' returns you. Generic equals invisible in AI-search era.
View velocity signal: views/hour first 24 hours vs your 20-post baseline. 0.5x-1.5x normal, 1.5-3x consider paid, 3x+ winner (amplify within 48 hrs).
Platform algorithm review: must happen monthly, not yearly. One hour reading release notes and creator updates keeps current.
Trend freshness floor: 14 days max age on audio, meme, reference. Anything older reads as late.
Budget pivot: shift from 80 media/20 creative to 50/50. Organic experimentation needs funding equivalent to paid amplification spend.
Content split: 80 percent structural (core niche, known for), 20 percent cultural (off-niche, discovery engine). Without 20 percent, invisible to new people.
Paid spend rule: 80 percent to validated winners only, 20 percent to exploration (new platforms/formats/segments). Never split even across unvalidated.
Amplification timing: within 48 hours of 3x+ baseline velocity for max lift. After day 7, substantially less efficient.
Comment quality signal: threaded conversations highest value. Short emoji comments means content performed but did not provoke.

Niche intersection rule: non-competitive market at intersection of two unrelated skills. Sourdough shipping (not bread), wedding photography on medium format only, lawyers+portrait (one industry vertical).
100-Video Rule: produce 100 authentically, ignore counts, sort by reach, top 5-10 cluster around 1-2 topics = intersection algorithm identified.
Maybe Filter: replace automatic no with 'maybe 90 days with capped loss (500 dollars, 20 hours, or both)'. Test hypothesis with downside clear.
Pebble-to-Boulder sequence: each stage funds and validates next. 25-99 dollar pebble proves demand before 300 dollar small boulder.

Service model specifics: Local AI agency (500-2,000/mo social + content + ads), Organic-to-paid pipeline (percentage of ROI), Live commerce setup (1,500-5,000/mo retainer), Content sprint (5,000-15,000 fixed), AI systems build (10,000-50,000 for midsized).
Live commerce 80/20: 80 percent education (technique, critique, Q&A), 20 percent pitching. One product pinned per session, mention every 10-15 minutes.
Email list ownership: newsletter with same-day weekly cadence becomes routine. Direct subscriber access survives algorithm change. Monetize when 5,000+ free subscribers.
Community over virality: 500-subscriber newsletter at 60 percent open rate more valuable than 50,000-follower 0.2 percent engagement account. Track repeat buyers, referral rate, comment depth.
Follower-to-view ratio Interest Media test: ratio >1 signals algorithm pushing to non-followers. Below 0.3 means creative failing test, 0.3-1 normal, 1-5 strong, 5+ breakout.
AI limitations: AI does not shoot, direct subjects, make creative decisions during shoot, build relationships, know what is not captured, or have taste. Photographer taste is load-bearing.
AI search prep: publish 200 pieces on clear niche > 'Bryceden Jones' in agent search. 10 pieces mixed-niche equals invisible. Content from 2024-2025 still training data 2027.
Hook categories: Contrarian statement, Specific result, Question viewer asks, Before-and-after promise, Visual surprise. Each tests 3-5 variations.
Batch capture types: Voice notes, Meeting recordings, Process footage from shoots, Phone-captured thoughts during commute.

Platform cutdown AI processing: 'Act as content editor. Adapt this transcript into 7 platform posts: LinkedIn text, LinkedIn image caption, Instagram Reels script, TikTok script, YouTube Shorts script, X thread, Substack intro.'

Platform posting cadence lock: LinkedIn 1 image post weekday at 7-9 AM (2-hr engagement window, repost if no traction), Instagram 4-7 Reels/week + daily Stories, TikTok 2-5/week minimum, YouTube Shorts same as Reels, Facebook 3-5/week (1-second loops), Substack 1/week same day, X varies daily, Whatnot/TikTok Live 2-5/week 30-60 min.

Portfolio ranking by attention/competition: LinkedIn (most underpriced), TikTok (less saturated than Instagram, algorithm merit-based), YouTube Shorts (underpriced, long-tail index), Substack (effectively empty for photographers), Whatnot/TikTok Live (portrait/commercial rarely there), Instagram Reels (saturated but default for photographers), Facebook (overlooked but spending demographic), X (network value only, not client conversion).
Solo photographer volume minimum: start 70/30 media-creative transitional, move to 60/40 after 90 days, arrive 50/50 by month 6.

Monetization layer funnel: Top of funnel (hook-heavy, broad, high-shareability discovery), Middle of funnel (longer videos, case studies, service connection to needs, MOST CREATORS SKIP THIS), Bottom of funnel (direct offers, pitches, consultations, limited-time). Every piece needs clear next step: newsletter signup, free guide, waitlist, consultation link.

Single-platform depth model validity: only when volume model burned out AND business needs smaller high-value audience. Test: has photographer tried volume and burned out, AND business depend on 500-200 right-fit people? If yes, depth model. If no, run volume first for data.

Conversion from volume to depth: after 6-12 months volume, identify Niche of One via 100-Video Rule, shift 70-80 percent effort to single platform for depth, maintain minimum presence (cutdowns) on others, review balance every 6 months.

contradictions: High volume (4-15 posts daily) vs solo photographer with demanding craft (wedding shooters 40/year cannot produce 15 daily without hiring or reducing shoot quality). Resolved: book acknowledges in Part XI counter-view that volume hurts when main craft is demanding; single-platform depth model is alternative for specific cases.

Generic category content (80 percent structural niche) vs algorithm preference for novelty/trends (requires 20 percent cultural off-niche). Not a contradiction; positioned as two-part system: 80 percent why they stay, 20 percent discovery engine.

Platform-native requirement vs efficiency of batch-processing one core content into seven cutdowns. Not a contradiction; batch process creates one core, then AI adapts each platform natively from that core.

Maybe Filter (test 90 days with capped loss) vs 12-month minimum commitment for visible compounding (Elephant Meeting section states month 3 is too early). Resolved: Maybe Filter is for platform/format experimentation at month scale; compounding of full system requires 12 months, not individual bets.

Community over virality (goal is 50-200 deeply engaged clients) vs operating at 4-15 posts per day across 7-9 platforms (designed for massive reach). Resolved: book clarifies both views in 11.5 sequence: run volume 6-12 months, then shift to depth; two phases, not opposition.
weird_gold: Interest Media rephrasing: 'A viewer who spent 30 seconds on portrait video last week sees your portrait video this week, regardless of follow status. Brand new account can out-perform 2M-follower legacy account.' Reframes entire social metric hierarchy.
Rough documentation 10:1 outperformance ratio: specific claim that rough phone setup footage beats cinematic video at 10:1 view ratio. Cuts against all photographer instinct about production value.
View velocity vs total views: leading indicator (views/hour first 24h) vs lagging indicator (absolute views). Enables quick 48-hour amplification window decision.
Hook testing delta: 5-20x view spread between best and worst hook on same content. Means hook is essentially the content.
Follower-to-view ratio >1 as Interest Media test: simple numerical gate (views divided by followers) determines algorithm health.
LinkedIn image over video (as of 2024): 4-8 line caption on static image outperforms video on currently-highest-opportunity platform.
TikTok algorithm as merit-based level playing field: new zero-follower account can hit hundreds of thousands views. Follower count irrelevant.

Niche of One example specificity: 'sourdough shipping' vs 'bread,' 'wedding photography exclusively on medium format film,' 'portrait photography for lawyers and law firms.' Non-obvious intersections.
1-second Facebook videos currently over-performing: very short loop with visual punch as discovery vehicle on overlooked platform.
Local-to-national via shippable product: photographer with local service business extends nationally via preset pack or print series pinned in live commerce, drives relative word-of-mouth referrals.
Pebble presell validates boulder: 200 copies at 30 dollars of pebble proves demand before expanding same topic to 300-dollar course.
Platform algorithm shifts three times in five years: active change rate makes 'best practices' from 2015 actively wrong.
Context injection as core AI skill: 5-13 minute voice note with business detail produces publishable AI output without editing. Generic prompts produce generic AI output.
Comment depth threaded conversations as platform highest-value signal: viewer reply-to-reply indicates content sparked community, not just performance.
Maybe Filter caps: '500 dollars, 20 hours, 90 days' as specific discipline against automatic-no cynicism.
50-100 hour AI learning minimum: hands-on use for real work produces prompt intuition that makes tools actually useful (not reading about tools).
9 PM-midnight window as asymmetric upside: three hours zero-consumption into pure creation for photographers with day jobs compounds into parallel career/business over 24-36 months.
100-Video Rule without peak bias: produce 100 authentically across full range, ignore counts, cluster identifies algorithm-discovered intersection (usually surprises creator's own niche guess).

Elephant Meeting remedy: open Instagram/TikTok, search own name, look at thousands of uncontrolled user-generated posts about you/category, realize brand control ended around 2010 (cannot control, only participate or hide).
